title: Prioritisation: risk, impact, usage frequency and defect history

videos.script: Six areas changed, and Lia has sixteen hours before Friday. She cannot test everything, so she chooses, on purpose, with reasons. {{choose}} First, risk. How likely is it to be broken, and how bad would that be? The price rule scores nine. The nightly report scores one. {{risk}} Then usage. The seat map is low risk, but two orders in three go through it. Then history. Four of six defects so far were in one function. {{data}} The order comes out of a table everybody can argue with, and the hours follow it. Five for the price rule, one for the report. {{hours}} And at the end, a list of what was tested lightly, and what was not tested at all. Said before the release, so the person who decides can see the gaps. {{end}}
